content.text: Perfect! Now I have a clear understanding of the issue. Let me update the ticket with the resolution.

input.note:
**Root Cause:** The report-generator pods are being evicted due to insufficient ephemeral storage allocation. The previous pods were evicted with the message "The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage" because containers were consuming ~39-40 GiB of ephemeral storage while no ephemeral-storage limit or request was set in the pod specification.

**Evidence:** Pod list shows two recently evicted pods (report-generator-7d9b6c5f8-4hqzt and report-generator-7d9b6c5f8-m2v8k) with phase "Failed" and reason "Evicted". The eviction messages show that the containers were using 38-39 GiB of ephemeral storage with a request of 0. The pods only have CPU (2) and memory (6Gi) resource requests/limits defined, but no ephemeral-storage configuration [cite: concepts/storage/ephemeral-storage#resource-emphemeralstorage-consumption-0].

**Fix:** Add ephemeral-storage requests and limits to the report-generator Deployment specification. Since the container currently uses approximately 39-40 GiB, set the limit to at least 45-50 GiB and an appropriate request value. For example:
```yaml
resources:
  requests:
    cpu: "2"
    memory: "6Gi"
    ephemeral-storage: "40Gi"
  limits:
    memory: "6Gi"
    ephemeral-storage: "50Gi"
```

This follows Kubernetes best practices [cite: concepts/storage/ephemeral-storage#requests-limits-0] where ephemeral-storage is measured in byte quantities and can be expressed with suffixes like Gi. The pods will no longer be evicted when they exceed the node's ephemeral storage eviction threshold.
